title: Why Early People Made Art
objective: After this level you can compare the main ideas about why early humans made art.
summary: Why early people made art is debated. Main ideas: an urge to record the world, hunting magic (with a reindeer problem), a spirit world, and keeping records.

cards.headline: Nobody left a note explaining the cave paintings.
cards.body: So researchers work from clues, and they disagree. The purpose of this art is still debated. Here are the main ideas. Hold them as ideas, not answers.

cards.headline: Idea: because people need to
cards.body: One view skips usefulness altogether: humans have a basic need to record and recreate the world around them. On this view the first artists drew for the same deep reason you doodle in a meeting. The catch is that it's hard to test.

cards.headline: Idea: hunting magic
cards.body: Maybe painting an animal was a kind of spell, to make a hunt succeed or herds multiply. It has a big problem at Lascaux. The bones left behind show the painters mostly ate reindeer, yet reindeer are almost absent from the walls. If you're casting a spell for dinner, you'd paint dinner.

cards.headline: Idea: a spirit world
cards.body: Most experts think cave art was symbolic or religious, sometimes both. One version: shamans entered trances to contact spirits, and the art shows that other world. Mixed creatures fit this idea, like Level 7's Lion-Man, or the Muna hand narrowed into a claw, which researchers think may reflect links between people and animals, or spiritual beliefs.

cards.fact: Some marks may be records, not pictures.
cards.context: Researchers suggest the patterns on an engraved ochre plaque from Blombos Cave may be a way of counting or storing information. Others wonder whether animals painted in their seasonal coats worked as an early calendar. The ideas don't have to compete: one cave could be a gallery, a temple and a notebook.

cards.headline: Why art: debated
learned: The purpose of prehistoric art is still debated
Hunting magic struggles with Lascaux's missing reindeer
Many experts see symbolic or religious meaning
Some marks may be records, like counts or calendars

questions.prompt: Match each idea about early art with how it explains the pictures.
questions.explanation: Hunting magic says painting was a spell to make a hunt succeed. The spirit world idea says shamans entered trances and painted that world. The records idea says some marks were a way of counting.

questions.prompt: Why do the food bones at Lascaux cause trouble for the hunting magic idea?

options.label: The bones are older than the paintings
options.rationale: The problem is which animals, not when.

options.label: The painters didn't eat meat at all
The bones show the animals were never hunted
options.rationale: Reindeer were clearly hunted and eaten.

options.label: The painters ate reindeer but barely painted them

questions.explanation: If paintings were spells for the hunt, you'd expect reindeer everywhere. Instead they're almost absent.

questions.prompt: Level 7's Lion-Man is part human, part lion. Which idea about early art does a creature like that fit best?

options.label: Records and counting
options.rationale: A lion-man doesn't count or track anything.

options.label: Copying nature exactly
options.rationale: No such creature exists in nature.

questions.explanation: Creatures mixing human and animal fit the idea that early art showed a world of spirits and beliefs.
